title: A cholinergic hub in the nucleus accumbens gates opioid-reward learning.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: I retrieved the full PMC author manuscript (PMC13454963) including the complete Methods, and searched it for a data- or code-availability statement: there is none, and there is no GitHub, Zenodo, Dryad, figshare or OSF link anywhere in the text. The Europe PMC supplementary-files endpoint returned an explicit error ('Article with id PMC13454963 is not open access one'); the PMC supplementary PDF link returned a 1,817-byte 'Preparing to download' challenge page instead of the file. Zenodo API search (0 records) and DataCite DOI search (0 records) on the paper title and on 'naloxone DART' both returned nothing. Sample sizes quoted below were read directly from the Methods text I retrieved.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All numbers: conditioned place preference (CPP, a test of whether an animal learns to prefer a place where it got a drug) cohort of 30 mice (16 naloxone-DART, 14 control-DART); open-field and elevated-plus-maze cohort of 12 mice (6 + 6); microdialysis (sampling brain chemicals through a probe) cohorts of 30 mice for acetylcholine and 31 for dopamine; slice electrophysiology of 7-11 cells per condition. I could not open a single data file, so nothing was checked against the files.

a1_downloadable.note: No data exist to download. The manuscript has no data-availability or code-availability statement; the only attached item is a 1.3 MB supplementary PDF that PMC's download endpoint blocks and Europe PMC refuses ('not open access'). Zenodo and DataCite searches returned 0 records for this DOI/title.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable because no file exists. Even in principle the candidate label (CPP score) and the candidate feature (percent of cholinergic interneurons carrying tethered drug) live only inside figure panels, so both would have to be reconstructed by digitising plots.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs (histology images, 3D pose-tracking traces from DANNCE, microdialysis chromatography values) are described in Methods but none are deposited or referenced by accession.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated clearly in the text (mg/kg morphine, micromolar drug concentrations, normalised CPP score, normalised delta-acetylcholine) — but only in the text, since there are no files.

a5_enough_rows.note: The unit of analysis is the mouse. Largest cohort is 30 mice (CPP); open field is 12 mice; microdialysis 30-31 mice; slice recordings 7-11 cells per condition. Far below the ~400-row floor for classification, let alone ~1,500 for regression. Read from Methods.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <1 MB of summary numbers if they existed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem; the data would be a few hundred rows at most.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked — there is no download to compare the paper's counts against.

a8_label_provenance.note: The candidate label (CPP score) is a direct behavioural measurement from infrared beam-break timing, not another model's output; the candidate feature (histological target engagement) comes from independent immunostaining. Provenance is clean, which makes the absence of the files the more frustrating.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: with 30 mice and no released data, any model fitted here would describe a single Duke cohort and could not be distinguished from the sigmoid curve the authors already fitted by eye.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use how much of a brain cell population got a blocking drug to predict how strongly a mouse learned to like morphine.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-mouse records pairing a histology measurement (what percent of acetylcholine-releasing interneurons in the nucleus accumbens medial shell carry the tethered drug) plus sex and treatment group with that mouse's behaviour. Verified count: 30 mice in the main cohort, 12 in the open-field cohort.
plain_idea.predict: The conditioned place preference score — the change in fraction of time the mouse spends in the morphine-paired chamber, measured by infrared beam breaks over a 30-minute free-exploration session before and after six days of conditioning.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Opioid-addiction circuit labs would want a quantitative dose-of-target-engagement curve to plan how much receptor blockade is needed; but the paper already fits exactly that curve, and with 30 animals there is nothing an ML model can add.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: regress conditioned place preference score on histological target engagement across brain subregions (medial shell, core, septum) to find the engagement threshold that abolishes opioid reward learning. The authors already do this with a three-parameter sigmoid and a bootstrap confidence interval on 30 mice — the right statistical tool for that n — and no file is released to redo it.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; the project dies before any compute is needed because no data file is obtainable.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the per-cohort n in the Methods. It took two minutes and returned 30 mice for the largest experiment — an immediate A5 failure independent of the missing files.

verdict_reason: Fails A1 and A5. No data availability statement, no repository deposit (Zenodo and DataCite return zero records), and both supplementary-file endpoints are blocked, so nothing can be downloaded. Independently, the unit of analysis is the mouse and the largest cohort is 30 animals (12 in the open field), roughly fifty times below the row count needed. This is an excellent circuit-neuroscience paper and a poor ML candidate: the measurements are clean, causal and well-controlled, but there are only tens of them and they exist solely inside figure panels.
